about.title: Rio Vista Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Vista's mix of agricultural operations, marina work, and small commercial trades along River Road and Main Street means workplace injuries here can look different than in a big city office park. A dockworker hurt loading equipment, a farmhand injured by faulty machinery, or a delivery driver struck near Rt-12 may all face the same confusing first question: who's responsible? In California, workers' compensation is usually the exclusive path against your employer, but if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Rio Vista workers with an independent attorney who can sort through which path, or paths, apply to your situation. There's no pressure and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Rio Vista Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Off the Table
items.desc: Even though workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — may still be liable, giving you a separate path to pursue.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early On
items.desc: California requires injuries be reported to your employer within 30 days, so timing can affect your options; an attorney can help you understand what's already been done and what's next.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Is the Law
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an independent attorney can help you understand your rights if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I work seasonal agricultural jobs near Rio Vista — does workers' comp still apply to me?
items.answer: In most cases, yes — California workers' compensation generally covers agricultural and seasonal employees just as it does other workers. An independent attorney can review your specific employment situation to confirm coverage and explain how to move forward. This is exactly the kind of question LawProactive can help connect you on.

items.question: What if my injury happened because of faulty equipment, not just an accident?
items.answer: If defective equipment or machinery contributed to your injury, you may have a claim against the equipment manufacturer or maintenance company separate from your workers' comp claim. These third-party claims follow a 2-year deadline in California, so it helps to look into this sooner rather than later. An attorney can evaluate whether this applies to your situation.

items.question: Can I still get help if my injury didn't happen during a big crash on Rt-12 or River Road?
items.answer: Absolutely — workplace injuries don't need to involve a vehicle collision to qualify for workers' comp or a third-party claim. Whether you were hurt on a job site, in a warehouse, or handling equipment, what matters is how and where the injury occurred. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney regardless of how the incident happened.
